entities.name: Levodopa
observations: Acute oral levodopa/carbidopa 250/25 mg increased absolute resting scalp alpha and beta power 60 minutes after dosing in 24 patients with probable Parkinson disease.
Acute levodopa decreased human subthalamic low-beta (13–20 Hz) activity, while alpha-band changes were not significant in an invasive LFP study.

entities.name: Parkinson disease
observations: Human studies assessed acute dopaminergic effects on scalp EEG and subthalamic oscillations in patients with Parkinson disease.

entities.name: PMID:25452725 Babiloni
observations: In 24 patients with probable Parkinson disease, oral levodopa/carbidopa 250/25 mg followed by a 60-minute interval significantly increased eyes-closed resting absolute alpha and beta power, mainly over centro-temporo-parietal derivations; delta and theta did not change.
Beta-power increases correlated negatively with rigidity and bradykinesia, while alpha increases showed a smaller negative correlation with resting tremor.

entities.name: PMID:24273711 Weinberger
observations: Compared with medication OFF, dopaminergic medication reduced resting cortical beta coherence and increased task-related beta power during successful stopping and going; this did not establish a global resting absolute-power change.

entities.name: PMID:26594626 Hohle
observations: In 12 patients with Parkinson disease, levodopa reinstated a more normal post-stimulus cortical beta-modulation profile during fast rhythmic auditory stimulation; the accessible report did not isolate a levodopa-specific resting alpha/beta power change.

entities.name: PMID:15380487 Priori
observations: After medication withdrawal, acute levodopa significantly decreased low-beta activity in human subthalamic nuclei; global alpha-band changes were not significant. This was invasive STN LFP power rather than scalp EEG.

entities.name: Scalp EEG alpha/beta response
observations: A single direct resting scalp-EEG study supports acute levodopa-related increases in absolute alpha and beta power, but other studies show measure-dependent beta effects rather than a uniform direction.

entities.name: Scaphocephaly
observations: An elongated, narrow skull with prominent occiput and broad forehead is concerning for sagittal craniosynostosis rather than typical positional plagiocephaly; diagnosis requires focused head-shape and suture examination.

entities.name: Sagittal craniosynostosis
observations: Isolated sagittal synostosis can present without neurologic or facial abnormalities; persistent or suspicious scaphocephaly merits prompt craniofacial/neurosurgical assessment, with imaging generally specialist-directed when examination is equivocal.

entities.name: Positional plagiocephaly
observations: Typical initial management is supervised tummy time while awake, alternating head position, reducing prolonged occipital pressure, and treating torticollis if present; routine imaging is unnecessary when examination is typical.

entities.name: Familial macrocephaly
observations: A rise from the 50th to 90th head-circumference percentile alone does not establish hydrocephalus; repeat accurate measurements, review the growth curve, and measure parental head circumferences.

entities.name: Hydrocephalus
observations: Hydrocephalus is more concerning when rapid head growth accompanies vomiting, lethargy, poor feeding, bulging fontanelle, abnormal eye movements, seizures, or developmental abnormalities; these are absent in this scenario.
